passages.note: Roll call 520: Donato voted Yea on the Conference Committee Report for HB 1447, a multi-subject education bill.
passages.tally_quote: HB 1447 - Donato Yea 39 Education matters. Nay 10 Conference Committee Report #1 Excused 0 Not Voting 1

passages.note: Bill details page lists Donato as Senate sponsor of HB 1447, a multi-subject education bill whose published digest covers third-party survey privacy, not library books.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Stacey Donato, Sen. Jeff Raatz.

passages.provision_quote: (2) procedure for each school to allow a: (A) parent or guardian of a student enrolled in the school; or (B) community member: (i) within the school district; or (ii) within the school district in which the charter school is located; to submit a request to remove material from the school library that is obscene (as described in IC 35-49-2-1) or harmful to minors (as described in IC 35-49-2-2); and (3) response and appeal procedure for each school to respond to a removal request submitted by a parent, guardian, or community member described in subdivision (2).
passages.note: New Chapter 5.5 lets both parents and community members request removal of library material, reviewed by the governing body at its next meeting; this mixes the rung-5 community-member trigger with a rung-3-like review step rather than matching either rung cleanly.

rows.reasoning: HB 1447 (2023) is a multi-subject education bill covering third-party survey privacy, Muncie school flexibility, political neutrality, and obscenity-law amendments in addition to the new school-library chapter, so Donato's Yea vote and Senate sponsorship show direction at most without a statement tying her act to the library provision specifically. That provision itself lets 'a parent or guardian' or 'a community member... within the school district' submit a removal request for obscene or harmful-to-minors material, reviewed by the governing body at its next public meeting, which mixes the rung-5 community-member trigger with a rung-3-like review step rather than matching any single rung's full clause set to the exclusion of the others.
